title: Sequence priming cost model and dynamic prefetch efficiency reporter
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: Priming (prefix tokens / user context reuse) reduces compute but introduces memory and KV cache pressure that affects both latency and tail-cost under mixed workloads. This PR introduces a lightweight cost model for sequence priming that estimates per-request marginal token cost given KV cache hit rates and sequence overlap, and a dynamic prefetch efficiency reporter that correlates priming heuristics, prefetch decisions, and observed GPU memory churn. Design: 1) cost_model.py implements an approximate amortized cost estimator that consumes per-cohort median sequence overlap, avg_kv_hit_rate, and batch composition to produce per-request cost delta. 2) prefetch_reporter.py hooks into the bench runner telemetry pipeline to record prefetch decisions, memory high-water marks, and per-epoch inference token throughput; it exports an aggregated CSV and a compact JSON summary for downstream dashboard ingestion. 3) Introduced a small controller in bench_runner to simulate two priming policies (conservative: prefetch only on >85% overlap; aggressive: prefetch on >40%) and evaluate cost/latency tradeoffs across sequence mixes. Results summary: synthetic runs across three seq-mix profiles (chatty, long-form, mixed) show the cost model predicts observed token-cost within 7-12% median error; aggressive prefetch reduces p50 latency by 6-9% on chatty profiles but increases GPU memory churn and p95 by 3-5% in mixed profiles. Backward compatibility: no runtime changes to production serving; this is a bench-only analysis toolchain. Checklist: - [x] unit tests for cost estimator and reporter CSV export - [x] integration run reproducer (bench scripts + recorded traces) - [x] perf baseline attached and archived - [x] documentation: bench/priming.md and example config. How to run: ./bench/runner.py --profile seq-mix-v2 --priming-policy aggressive --out results/priming-aggressive.csv Notes: results include attached flamegraphs for memory allocation hotspots and a short howto to translate CSV output into Redwood Console ingestion format. Related: informs ENG-3192 (priming rollout guidance) and will feed into cost-aware routing experiments.
